reported_success.quote: ﬁndings replicate that of Barrett et al. (2010), in which arousal ... positively predicted nostalgia rating, indicating that more nostalgic ... songs were experienced as higher arousal.

notes: Identity verified independently: supplied text has matching title Unique Affective Profile of Music-Evoked Nostalgia: An Extension and Conceptual Replication of Barrett et al.’s (2010) Study, authors Sarah Hennessy, Timothy Greer, Shrikanth Narayanan, Assal Habibi, and DOI 10.1037/emo0001389. It is the primary research article (2024 advance online publication), with Methods, Results, Discussion, tables and references through printed p.23; not merely an abstract. No PDF was supplied. Original side and unassigned fields are placeholders only. The requested standardized beta is not established: context variables were raw and not standardized; person scores were mean-centered, not described as standardized. Printed β coefficients and Cohen’s f² candidates are retained without conversion. Context models distinguish high arousal (β=3.89, t(1681)=39.27, adjusted p<.001, f²=0.49) and low arousal (β=0.08, adjusted p>1, f² approximately 0.00), Table 5 p.7. Locator does not specify high versus low. The authors model arousal as outcome and nostalgia/control as categorical predictor, rather than nostalgia ratings as outcome. Common candidate-model sample is explicitly N=582 participant clusters and 2,234 song observations. It is retained only as a candidate because row-to-test mapping is unresolved. Participants with improper responses (14) or no matched control songs (172) were excluded; unmatched song pairs were excluded. No N was inferred from df and no arithmetic sum was used.
